The effect of emotion on tactile duration perception

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the effect of emotion on duration judgments depends on the nature of the emotion and the temporal range of the bisection task.
the duration of emotional events is modulated by emotional stimuli in other modalities, and that this modulation is not solely due to arousal.
the modulation of tactile duration by emotional pictures can be explained in terms of the crossmodal linkage between the visual and the tactile systems.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
emotional regulation is a crucial factor in the crossmodal modulation of tactile duration judgments.
the emotional valence of visual stimuli can modulate the perception of tactile duration.
duration judgments of tactile stimuli are modulated by emotion in the visual modality.
The main takeaway from our work is that
emotional regulation is not a unitary process, and the emotional valence and arousal of stimuli need to be carefully distinguished when investigating the impact of emotion on time perception.
the emotional content of a stimulus can influence the perception of a stimulus in another sensory modality.
emotional stimuli can affect duration perception in a crossmodal way, and this modulation is dependent on the range of the duration to be judged.
